Music, Save
Us Tonight

The story

This song leans into church before it leans into the club. The lead vocal is raspy and soulful, more testifying than singing, backed by a full choir that turns the hook into something closer to a chant than a chorus. At its core, it's classic four-on-the-floor house: punchy kick, crisp claps, a bassline that won't let go of the groove.

The arrangement does real work getting there, though — filter sweeps and risers pull the tension tight before every drop, so each chorus lands like relief. Underneath the party, it's really a song about needing something bigger than yourself to get through the night, and finding it in the people around you.
